title: Stop-hook check procedures
desc: T2 howto for the Stop hook: required-field contract, structural vs text-based checks, and per-check test recipes. Core: harness-stop-guard. History: harness-stop-guard-ref.
steps: THE FROZEN SPEC, OWNER 2026-09-07, AND THERE ARE NO MORE UPGRADES. Read this before touching anything in the Stop path, and treat every other step in this skill as subordinate to it. THE WHOLE GATE IS FOUR LINES. ONE, BLOCK FIRST AND PRINT THE STATUS. TWO, THE STATUS IS THE PACE LINE PLUS THE WISH LINE PLUS SKILL GUIDANCE TIERED BY SESSION SIZE, and nothing else. THREE, A CONSECUTIVE STOP IS ALLOWED -- the session was shown the frame, answered, and may rest. FOUR, EVERYTHING ELSE IS BLOCKED, and when the stop IS allowed the ball leaves the model entirely, going to the owner or to an external event such as an agent finishing. Owner, default-deny in his own words: if you are not sure, block it all, and accept only when you are certain. FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-09-08, rule THREE now works -- Get-WkStopConsecutive.ps1 asks whether a USER MESSAGE follows the last Stop notice instead of whether the session sat idle. THREE CASES RUN, and the negative control is REAL DATA rather than a fixture: a fixture holding Stop then two tool_use entries and no user message returns TRUE, this session own live transcript returns FALSE because the owner had spoken since the last stop, and an unreadable path returns FALSE so the documented fail direction survives. THE FLIP IS PROVEN rather than asserted: the OLD code hits the first tool_use in its window and returns false on that same fixture, so False became True. The original defect is kept below because the successor needs the shape of it. MEASURED DEFECT 2026-09-08, and rule THREE WAS NOT WORKING -- five consecutive stops in one session, 03:06, 04:06, 09:13, 09:19 and 12:38, every one BLOCKED. Test-WkStopConsecutive returns FALSE when called directly against that live transcript, so the allow arm never fires. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, and both make the allowance unreachable for any session that does work. FIRST, stop_hook_active is honoured at Get-WkStopFrameVerdict.ps1 line 28, but that flag's counter RESETS ON ANY TOOL CALL, which the file's own comment states -- so a session that runs one command between stops can never carry it. SECOND, the fallback window of three counts a user message OR A tool_use as earned-again, so the only allowed shape is stop, words-only reply, stop -- and a working session never produces it. THE OWNER'S TWO WORKED EXAMPLES ARE THE SPEC for that window and they are recorded correctly in the source. THE GAP IS THAT BOTH IMPLEMENTATIONS TEST FOR AN IDLE SESSION WHILE THE RULE MEANS A REPEATED STOP, so whoever fixes this must decide what CONSECUTIVE counts from -- the hook invocation itself, which is written on every call, allowed or blocked -- rather than from the absence of work. THE ACCOUNTING IS ALSO DEAD, same day, and it is a separate defect: tools/wkharness-claude-stop.ps1 contains ZERO calls to Write-WkStopDecisionLog, so the log that records BOTH block and allow wrote nothing today while carrying entries from the 6th and 7th. Repeat-block escalation reads those same files and returns false on a missing one, so it is disarmed too. Counted from the invocation log: 288 hook invocations today, 96 reaching the decision write, ZERO reaching the logger. THE REQUIRED-FIELD CONTRACT is the check you will hit most (temp diagnostic 2026-08-07: wkharness-guards-stop.ps1 ALLOW path got a one-line wkappbot speak marker, additive, try/catch-wrapped, remove once observed), and it is mechanical. A closing report must carry KNOWN_BUGS, EMERGENCY_ACTION, NEXT_REQUIRED_ACTION and COULD_NOT_VERIFY, each as an English label on its own line, colon, then a NON-EMPTY value written in the USER'S language. A bare header counts as missing. LAYER-FIXES 2026-08-28 (commits c2fd253d8, 1183afbac): [Fix 1] Exclude transcript entries 'Stop hook feedback:' or '<local-command-caveat>' from recitation—post-fix logs byte-identical across 4 blocks. [Fix 2] Extract Get-WkStopIdleSpinVerdict to flip Decision on 9-line idle-spin, fixing fixtures (script:WkStopTranscriptPath required, TAB-separated logs, DateTime::UtcNow). COULD_NOT_VERIFY is the one sessions try hardest to leave blank. DEBUGGING NOTE 2026-08-09, RESTORED 2026-08-28 after a delegate stripped its opening clause and left a headless fragment: when wiring a script-scope fallback (e.g. $script:WkStopSessionId) into a check function called by the registry dispatcher, an isolated unit test of the fallback expression can pass while the SAME expression inside the real function still fails -- always test end-to-end through the actual dot-sourced function, never trust an isolated copy of the logic as proof the wiring works. RELATED GOTCHA, same day: when verifying a check's PASS case through Invoke-WkStopCheckWithTimeout (the RunspacePool wrapper), the returned .Reason on a genuine pass is NOT literal $null -- EndInvoke() hands back a PSDataCollection, and comparing it with '$null -eq $result.Reason' silently reads as a FALSE FAIL even though the underlying check correctly returned null. Use '[string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($result.Reason)' instead, which correctly coerces the empty collection. Confirmed by adding debug output: the type was PSDataCollection, not $null, and IsNullOrWhiteSpace correctly read True.; filling it honestly is a PASS, not a confession, and leaving it empty is the single most common reason a turn will not close.

THE SUBSTANCE FLOOR IS NARROW, NOT A WORD COUNT. An earlier version rejected any field value under nine words, which falsely flagged honest short answers -- a bare commit hash, a suggest timestamp, the word 'fixed'. It now trips on only two things: an exact-match placeholder from a denylist (x, none, n/a, -, ?, unknown, tbd, todo and friends) or a value under three characters. Write a real short answer with confidence; do not pad it to satisfy a length rule that no longer exists.

COMPLETION CHECK: Wants specific DONE statement OR explicit open+next-action (40+ words). Both legitimate. Committed/verified/confirmed language required., or an explicit statement of what remains open PLUS the exact next action -- with committed/verified/confirmed language and at least forty words. Both halves are legitimate; an honest 'here is what is still broken and here is the exact next command' passes just as cleanly as a success report.

wk-stop-test ONLY EXERCISES THE STRUCTURAL GATES -- this is the trap, and it cost a real session a wrong conclusion on 2026-07-26. The tool's synthetic transcript does not present the message file's content as a scannable assistant text block, so the message-TEXT detectors (stop-menu offer, English bug-fix claim, Korean bug-fix claim) never see it. Proof already recorded: four semantically opposite messages returned the byte-identical BLOCK reason. So a BLOCK from wk-stop-test tells you the skill-search gate or the required-fields gate fired; it tells you NOTHING about whether a bug-claim detector would have caught the message.

TO ACTUALLY TEST A TEXT DETECTOR, use the -Test fixtures in wkharness-claude-stop.ps1 (see step 12 for baseline: PASS 12/26 measured 2026-07-26). byte-identical to the run with the changes applied, and all 14 failures read 'expected allow, got block' with zero block-to-allow regressions. The fixtures predate the required-fields contract (grep finds the string KNOWN_BUGS in none of them), so they assert a contract the gate no longer honours. Re-measure the HEAD baseline before attributing any failure to your own change, and never update a fixture's expectation to match new behaviour without that baseline in hand. Reach for wk-stop-test only when the question is about the structural gates. Getting this backwards produces a confident, evidence-shaped, wrong answer -- which is worse than no answer, because it closes the investigation.

CHECK INVENTORY: Registry=tools/wkharness-guards-stop-checks.ps1 (Test-WkStopCheck* functions). Skill-search gate + completion-marker live in wkharness-guards-stop.ps1 itself (not registry). A block may list every reason at once, not first only.

A BLOCK LISTS EVERY REASON AT ONCE, not the first one. Read all of them before fixing anything -- a session that fixes only reason 1 and retries gets blocked again on reasons 2 and 3 and starts to read the gate as capricious.

NAVIGATION: the design rationale and dated build history are in harness-stop-guard-ref; the parent reflex list is harness-stop-guard; the discipline of proving a detector fires rather than assuming it does is verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static.

THE PRE-CHECK NOW INCLUDES THE REFLECTION SCORE, which is the half I shipped without and had to be told about twice. Test-WkStopCheckNextDispatchBlockers listed LOW REFLECTION in its docstring from the first commit while only the dirty-tree and unpaid-pulse halves were actually coded -- a docstring is not an implementation, and the gap survived because the function looked complete. WHY THIS PARTICULAR BLOCKER MATTERS MOST: agent-debrief-gate refuses every dispatch when the governing reflection scores under 70, and that score DRIFTS DOWN ON ITS OWN, because each knowledge-op merges a step back from HQ and every added step divides the score through the oversize term. A session is therefore delegation-capable on one turn and refused on the next without anyone touching a reflection deliberately -- measured today going 77, 71, 67 across ordinary honest edits. The check now reports any of the three model reflections that has fallen under threshold, and names the CORRECT remedy rather than the reflex one: not --add-step, which makes an oversize skill worse, but a trim or a move of dated incidents into the -ref sibling. VERIFY THE MOVE REACHED HQ BEFORE TRIMMING THE CORE -- the first attempt today wrote 51 steps into the ref, reported success with a 100/100 reward, and a grep of the HQ copy found none of it, so trimming at that moment would have left those lessons in a single repo-local file. Fail-open on a missing scorer: an unavailable score is not evidence of a low one.

INCIDENTS 2026-07-26: Early allow bypass in NudgeDecision (consolidated from step 22), and fixture-to-live mismatch where fixture newlines vs real carriage-returns broke text detector unit tests -- unit tests passed isolated but detectors stayed inert live. Root: the test fixture construction used real newlines while file newlines from Stop's actual transcript capture were CRLF. Unit test passed, live test failed, and the gap persists until  wk-stop-test exercises the live Stop entry point (not just structural gates). See wkharness-claude-stop.ps1 -Test fixtures for the detector paths (step 12).. Get-WkStopNudgeDecision had three exits: no-tool-call branch skipped recency, completion, skill-gate checks. See 23 for negated-field issue. -- a turn closed on 2026-07-26 carrying a phrase the list already contained and the gate approved it, so adding more phrases would have changed nothing. Get-WkStopNudgeDecision had THREE exits: the no-tool-call branch owned its own block AND its own allow, and that allow ran two checks before approving, so the turn that did the least work took a private path to success and never met the recency, completion, skill-gate, negated-field or next-action checks. The split approve log shows that branch producing the most approvals in the file. WHEN: a detector you can prove fires synthetically did not fire in production, or you are about to widen a phrase list because a gate let something through. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto and read the approve-log reason field for that exact turn -- it names the branch that approved, and 'no tool call this turn' means every check below it was skipped -- then run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static before trusting either result. WHY: the function now collapses to ONE success return at the bottom, the branch seeds its findings into the shared reason list and sets a work-excused flag, and only the three checks that genuinely cannot judge a toolless turn are excused as individual checks -- proving that a gate which never ran looks exactly like a gate whose vocabulary was too narrow, and only the log distinguishes them.

(Merged with duplicate step 11) Fixtures predate required-fields contract. Reach for wk-stop-test only when the question is about the structural gates. Getting this backwards produces a confident, evidence-shaped, wrong answer -- which is worse than no answer, because it closes the investigation.

INCIDENT (2026-07-26): Unit probe passed but detector inert live. Root: fixture had real newlines, turnText is raw JSON (backslash-n). Match never started due to killed word-boundary. LESSON: probe tests your idea of input, not the input itself., because the probe built its fixture with real newlines while turnText is RAW JSON string content where a line break is the two characters backslash and n -- which left a word character against the field label and killed a leading word-boundary anchor, so the match never started. The probe passed for the wrong reason and would have shipped a dead guard as verified. WHEN: you have unit-tested any detector that consumes turnText, or a detector you can prove fires in isolation does not change a live verdict. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto then drive Get-WkStopNudgeDecision itself against a real .jsonl transcript and assert your reason STRING appears in the returned Reason, and put a known-good control in the same run -- the pre-existing forbidden-word case appearing while the new one stayed absent is what located the fault inside the check rather than in the wiring. WHY: measured 2026-07-26, the two runs disagreed completely on the identical input, so a fixture you construct yourself tests your idea of the input rather than the input, and only the real transcript carries the JSON escaping the detector actually meets.

TODO/VERIFICATION: Stop-logs health check. RUN: -Test tail + list USERPROFILE/.claude/wkharness-stop-logs. PROOF OF HEALTH: tail shows PASS n/N AND log file updated after measurement start. PROOF OF BROKEN: -Test errors OR logs unchanged. INVARIANT (step 37): mid-turn user interjection never reaches Stop yet. then list USERPROFILE/.claude/wkharness-stop-logs with name, length and last-write time. PROOF that the hook is HEALTHY: the self-test tail prints a PASS n/N line AND a stop-approve or stop-block file carries a last-write time later than the moment the measurement began. PROOF that it is BROKEN: the self-test errors, or no log file changes despite a decision being produced. INVARIANT: a turn that is continued by a mid-turn user message never reaches Stop, so an absence of log lines across a stretch of such turns is expected and is NOT evidence of an outage -- that ambiguity is exactly what this measurement exists to remove. WHEN: log files show no new lines for hours while the session has clearly been ending responses. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto for the check inventory, then delegate the two commands as a measurement-only dispatch and re-run them at ROOT before believing the result. WHY: measured 2026-07-27, ROOT raised a fleet-wide outage alarm from an empty log and had to retract it, because the queue-operation turns it had been having never produced a stop to record.

TODO: at STOP, run a DELEGATION-READINESS dry-run and refuse the stop when the session is not immediately delegatable. CONTRACT: evaluate the dispatch gate chain against a synthetic minimal-compliant Haiku brief in EVALUATE-ONLY mode -- freshness, tier-gate, brief-guard, clean-baseline, busy-fleet, debrief and pulse -- and SPAWN NOTHING, so the check costs no tokens and stays sub-second. If any gate refuses, BLOCK the stop and name that gate plus its own remedy line. PROOF that it works: with a reflection scored under seventy the stop is refused naming the freshness gate, and after that score is restored the identical turn closes. FAIL-SAFE: an error inside the evaluation BLOCKS, matching the read-failure paths. WHEN: wiring the stop side of the relax-input tighten-stop direction. HOW: run wkappbot skill read agent-debrief-gate-howto for the gate inventory and the one-turn-licence design it pairs with, then build it as a proto with its own self-test before touching canonical. WHY: measured 2026-07-27, a session ended turn after turn while every delegation path was locked and nothing forced it to repair that, so the successor inherited a fleet it could not use -- a session must not be allowed to close leaving delegation broken for whoever comes next.

BUG (2026-07-27, merged incident): Refusal did not fire for Korean denial + live blocked-build. Probe shows green (4/4), but actual transcript had different wording. Always use real transcript (not fixture) per verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static. that answered EMERGENCY_ACTION with the Korean denial while KNOWN_BUGS listed a live blocked build, and that report reached the user. WHEN: auditing whether that refusal fires in production, or about to widen its vocabulary because something got through. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the drive-the-real-thing procedure, then drive Get-WkStopNudgeDecision against a REAL transcript carrying that wording with the forbidden-word case as a known-good control in the same run. WHY: the call site sits in the same prepend block as the forbidden-word check, and that check demonstrably DID fire for the same session at 02:07Z, so the enclosing block executed and only this one stayed quiet. AND MY OWN PROBE PROVES LESS THAN IT LOOKS: I drove the sub-check directly with four variants including the verbatim wording, got the refusal 4 of 4 and silence on a healthy value, and built every fixture with REAL newlines -- precisely the trap the earlier incident in this skill records, since turnText is raw JSON where a line break is the two characters backslash and n, and a leading word-boundary anchor already died that way once. So the green result tests my idea of the input, not the input. Record no cause until one is reproduced: the candidates are that the blocked turn and the delivered turn were different turns, or that the label and its value never meet in the same scanned text.

INCIDENT: NEXTACTION ANCHOR (merged with step 28): Farms TODO without enforcing execution. step 28 provides QUOTATION-TIE fix. in the SAME anchor (Classify-NextAction, tools/wkharness-guards-stop-nextreadiness.ps1 lines 17-39, found 2026-08-09): it recognizes ONLY 3 shapes (delegation: Agent|delegate|dispatch|wkcodex|codex; 'wkappbot skill read|add|edit'; 'git commit|push') and hard-blocks EVERYTHING else as UNCLASSIFIED -- including wkappbot suggest list/resolve, git log/status/diff, wkappbot file edit -- regardless of whether the declared action was actually executed that same turn (confirmed live: running the exact declared command as a real tool call immediately before closing still hit UNCLASSIFIED). Workaround: phrase NEXT_REQUIRED_ACTION using one of the 3 recognized shapes even when the honest next step is a read-only command. Fix direction: add a READ_ONLY_COMMAND class (suggest list/show/check, git log/status/diff/show, skill search) that always passes precondition since read-only actions have no readiness gate to fail. without ever committing to the action, because the anchor asks only whether a TODO for that skill was recorded anywhere in the turn, not whether that TODO IS the action. WHEN: reviewing a report whose NEXT_REQUIRED_ACTION is a bare 'wkappbot skill read <id>', or auditing why a weak report closed. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkharness-guards-howto for the anchor's decision history, then dot-source tools/wkharness-skill-policy.ps1 and tools/wkharness-guards-stop-nextaction.ps1 and call Test-WkNextActionAnchor with a turn whose recorded TODO is deliberately unrelated to the declared action. WHY: measured 2026-07-27 -- a sibling's report REFUSES on its own with 'no TODO step was recorded for it in this turn', but a turn carrying 'TODO: buy milk, unrelated to the action' beside 'NEXT_REQUIRED_ACTION: wkappbot skill read <that same id>' PASSES outright; and the skill that was fed shows the tell, four near-duplicate TODOs added the same day, one of whose own WHY states the purpose as keeping the item visible to the stop guard's per-turn check. That is knowledge written for the gate rather than for a successor, and it inflates step count, dragging the fed skill's tier score toward the blocking threshold, so the abuse damages the catalog while it passes. The structural fix is the QUOTATION tie: require a verbatim run of the recorded TODO inside the declared action, so a TODO that is not the action cannot pay for it.

(Merged: secondary optimization after QUOTATION-TIE fix for step 16 anchor.) WHEN: that module is next opened, or the pre-commit wiring checker reports an indented dot-source on it again. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto for the check inventory, then move the wkharness-skill-policy.ps1 dot-source above the function definition and re-run the module's own -SelfTest from the canonical path plus the independent probe at .tmp/v3-independent-check.ps1. WHY: the checker flagged it on that module's own promotion commit 2026-07-27 and the flag is correct in general -- a dot-source inside a conditional branch runs only when that branch runs, which is exactly how a dependency silently fails to load and how this repo has already shipped one dead guard. Here it is deliberate, a fallback firing only when the caller forgot to load the resolver, so the commit passed on a warn; hoisting makes the load unconditional, removes the per-call cost, and leaves the checker with nothing to flag.

(Merged: module seam wiring step. Must be in receipt roster, not silent-skip.) so a missing module refuses instead of silently skipping. WHY: the seam wired 2026-07-27 follows the existing pattern of the other module seams -- if the module file is missing the whole block is skipped in silence -- which is precisely the skipped-is-not-passed failure the receipt ledger exists to make impossible, so leaving this check outside the roster reintroduces at one seam the exact hole the ledger closed everywhere else.

EMERGENCY_ACTION (WIRED/TODO): 23/23 pass, one failure (Korean -hal modifier + English vocab). step 20 interim. Both halves need Hangul lists before full wiring., 23 of 23 from the canonical path, after the Korean false-refusal was traced to PowerShell array-literal precedence rather than to the regex anchor I suspected. (Merged into EMERGENCY_ACTION step) Interim carve-out: skip action-half when Hangul present. WHEN: resuming the emergency-is-action proto, or writing any stop check that inspects report wording. PROOF: a Korean line reporting a completed act with no hash or skill id must PASS, while a Korean line ending in an intent ending must still REFUSE. WHY: measured 2026-07-27 the check refuses a Korean report because its vocabulary is English-only, and an interim carve-out that skips the action half whenever Hangul is present did not clear it, so the intent half is refusing too -- both halves need the same treatment and the interim skip is a placeholder, not the fix.

READINESS FIX (2026-07-27, CONFIRMED): Dot-source must sit immediately above call, not at module load. FIXED: could-not-be-established message stopped 08:53:01Z, zero instances in 31 blocks after (vs. every turn before)., not beside a sibling site. WHEN: a stop check reports it could not evaluate, or you move a seam earlier in the decision. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto for the check inventory, then put the guarded dot-sources of wkharness-common-skilllock, wkharness-guards-freshness-scope and wkharness-guards-agent-debrief directly above the call, and confirm by watching the block log stop carrying the could-not-be-established line. WHY: measured 2026-07-27 -- removing a duplicate readiness seam did NOT stop the message, and that is exactly what located the fault, because a message that survives deleting one of two callers belongs to the other. The surviving seam sits far earlier in the decision than the old pre-load did, so at call time the freshness resolver was undefined, the gate counted zero evaluable gates, and reported that as a block on every turn across three sessions. I walked into this trap twice in one day from opposite directions -- suspecting logic when a dependency was missing, then suspecting the dependency when a seam was duplicated -- and a probe cleared it both times, because a probe loads exactly what it needs and production does not.

RESULT: the readiness fix is CONFIRMED by count -- the could-not-be-established line stops at 08:53:01Z and appears in NONE of the 31 blocks recorded after it. WHEN: the next session opens, or any time the readiness gate is changed again. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto for the gate inventory, then read the stop-block log for the current day and count entries carrying that phrase, comparing the count before and after the 2026-07-27 dependency-order commit. PROOF: the phrase appears in blocks up to that commit and in none after it, while the approve log resumes recording allowed stops. WHY: a guard fire-rate is a recurrence score, so a fix is only proven by the count going to zero and staying there -- and this exact message survived my first fix, which is what proved the fault lay in the seam I had kept rather than the one I removed.

HYPHENATED TOKEN BUG (2026-07-27): Anchor requiring six consecutive words from TODO conflicts with prose containing hyphenated phrases. QUOTATION-TIE in step 16 fix: require actual TODO verbatim in action, narrows filter to real ids only., because the same field is required to QUOTE prose. WHEN: writing or reviewing any gate that harvests identifiers out of free text. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto for the anchor contract, then make the resolver a FILTER rather than a gate -- keep the tokens that resolve, refuse only when none do -- and re-run the module's self-test plus a probe of the original hole to prove the narrowing did not reopen it. WHY: measured 2026-07-27 on my own turn. The anchor demands the action value quote at least six consecutive words of the recorded TODO, and ordinary English inside a TODO is full of three-segment hyphenated phrases; quoting the phrase 'the could-not-be-established line' made the check read that phrase as a skill id and refuse the turn because no such skill exists on disk. TWO REQUIREMENTS OF ONE FIELD FOUGHT EACH OTHER -- quote the prose, and let every hyphenated thing in it be a real id -- and satisfying the first guaranteed failing the second. After the fix the fabricated-id case still refuses, and both original bypasses still refuse.

RESULT: the next-action anchor reads ASSISTANT TEXT ONLY, so it cannot see the skill-edit command that recorded the TODO -- which makes it satisfiable only by pasting that command into the visible message. WHEN: a turn is refused saying the recorded TODO is not adequately quoted even though the action value quotes it verbatim. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto and check where turnText comes from -- wkharness-guards-stop.ps1 around line 281 joins the type-text blocks and nothing else -- then either paste the recording command into the report or fix the extraction to scan tool_use input as well. WHY: measured 2026-07-27 across four consecutive turns of mine. I quoted thirteen consecutive words of a TODO I had just recorded and was still refused, because the recording happened in a TOOL CALL and tool calls are not text blocks, so the extraction had nothing to compare against. This answers the open question left in an earlier step about whether the anchor scans command lines. THE DESIGN CONSEQUENCE IS THE REAL FINDING: a check that can only be satisfied by narrating your own command rewards transcription rather than evidence, which is the shape this guard exists to refuse everywhere else.

NEXT-ACTION ANCHOR DESIGN (core rule: type-text only, step 1 invariant to prevent self-misread of hook's own commands): Cannot see tool-use-recorded TODOs. Must scan SKILL FILE ON DISK instead, or require verbatim quotation in message (step 16 QUOTATION-TIE). Scanning tool_use breaks a stated invariant: harness-stop-guard step 1 requires every detector here to read type-text blocks ONLY, because otherwise the hook misreads its OWN commands as the model's statements. WHEN: the anchor refuses a verbatim quotation, or you are about to paste your own command into a report purely to satisfy it. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto for the extraction finding, then widen the capture in wkharness-guards-stop.ps1 near line 281 to include tool_use input blocks alongside the text blocks, and prove it by recording a TODO in a tool call only and watching the anchor accept a quotation of it. PROOF: a turn whose skill-edit appears solely as a tool call, with the action quoting six consecutive words of that TODO, must pass. WHY: measured 2026-07-27 across five consecutive turns, the check compares against text it cannot see, so the only way through is transcription -- and rewarding a session for retyping its own command is the exact shape this guard refuses everywhere else.

READINESS MULTI-GATE (2026-07-27, NOT WIRED): Built but busy-fleet self-gather fails on live shape. Get-WkStopReadinessBlockReason with -TurnText ONLY returns could-not-be-read. Wiring would re-create fleet-wide block. Stashed as .tmp/nextreadiness-multigate-proto.ps1., because its busy-fleet self-gathering still fails on the hub's real call shape. WHEN: picking this item up, or judging any proto whose own suite is green. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-stop-guard-howto for the gate inventory, then call Get-WkStopReadinessBlockReason with -TurnText ONLY -- the way the hub calls it -- against a delegation-shaped next action, and read whether busy-fleet reports evaluated or could-not-be-read. WHY: measured 2026-07-27. The proto's own three critical cases pass because they STUB the resolver, and the real call still answers 'the busy-fleet gate could not be read'. The check already passes when the NOT_WIRED value carries a blocker word or a concrete file-and-line anchor; add a third branch that passes when a delegation was dispatched in this turn, resolved the same way busy-fleet already resolves it from the session jsonl rather than from any claim in the report. Scope the row ROOT-only, since a subagent has no fleet to feed. TWO GUARDRAILS, and the check is a trap without them. FIRST, ANY delegation satisfying it makes the gate payable by a FILLER dispatch, which is the same shape as the abuses this repo already blocks -- a bare-number like that reorders a step without quoting content, and the model-stamp spoof -- so at minimum log which dispatch paid it, and prefer a relatedness signal such as the unwired artifact's name appearing in the brief before tightening. SECOND, SOME WIRING CANNOT BE DELEGATED: it waits on ROOT review, on an owner decision, or on a measurement, and forcing a dispatch there manufactures a useless agent purely to satisfy a gate. OWNER DECISION 2026-08-01, which SIMPLIFIES this deliberately: do NOT build elaborate machinery for the blocker branch. Ship the simple half -- an unwired item with no delegation this turn refuses the stop -- and when that verdict is genuinely wrong for a case wiring cannot be delegated, the OWNER stops the session by hand. A human escape valve is stronger than a phrase list here, because a text branch that accepts naming-a-blocker is satisfied by prose, and prose is exactly what this session proved is free to invent. Keep the refusal text honest about that: say the gate is deliberately blunt and that a wrong verdict is expected to be overridden by the owner rather than argued past. PROOF: an unwired item with neither a delegation nor a blocker must BLOCK, the same item plus a real dispatch this turn must ALLOW, and the same item plus a blocker clause and no dispatch must also ALLOW. THREE FINDINGS FROM THE EXISTING RECORD, so none of this is re-derived. FIRST, this IS the tighten-the-stop half of an architectural direction already recorded -- agent-debrief-gate-howto states that a gate prescribing a remedy must licence it for one turn and COLLECT THE DEBT AT STOP rather than at the moment of the act, because a knowledge-op is always allowed while the dispatch is the very thing being blocked, and it names relax-the-input and tighten-the-stop as the correct direction. SECOND, the filler-dispatch worry is already half-solved upstream: busy-fleet ESCALATES after the first dispatch and explicitly refuses to count another read-this-and-report-back survey, demanding a prototype together with its own self-test, so this gate should REUSE that real-work discrimination rather than invent a relatedness check of its own. THIRD, and this bounds the whole design: every block costs a FULL-CONTEXT RE-SEND, which makes fire-rate a hard cost metric and a long session weight later blocks far heavier -- so this gate must stay narrow and always-satisfiable, and its fire-rate must be measured rather than assumed, because a rising count is evidence the embodiment is failing rather than working.

DECISION: THE UNWIRED SIGNAL BELONGS IN MORE PLACES THAN THE STOP GATE, and most of them are cheaper and earlier (owner 2026-08-01). WHEN: designing where any report-derived signal should live, not only this one. WHY THE STOP GATE IS THE WORST PLACE TO PUT IT: a block costs a FULL-CONTEXT RE-SEND, which makes it the single most expensive surface in the harness and weights later blocks in a long session far heavier; it fires LATE, after the work is already done; and it is BINARY, so it can only say no. HOW, in rough order of value. FIRST the busy-fleet refusal: it already orders ROOT to delegate, so having it NAME the currently unwired items turns a refusal into a WORK QUEUE -- same data, and the message changes from no into send this. SECOND session start: surface the predecessor's unwired inventory at on-load so a session MEETS it on the first screen instead of being punished for it on the last. THIRD the handoff letter: an unwired inventory is precisely what that document exists to carry, so it can be GENERATED rather than hand-written and stops depending on the retiring session remembering. FOURTH a PostToolUse nudge, which is free and non-blocking and rides in additionalContext where the model actually reads it. FIFTH repo health: an unwired count is a health metric of the same kind as the garbage collector's unused-file count. SIXTH the dispatch brief itself, where the oldest unwired item is the obvious candidate sector. THE GENERAL RULE WORTH CARRYING: reach for a BLOCK only when the behaviour must be impossible; for everything else the same signal is cheaper and lands earlier as a nudge, a queue entry, or a line in the letter -- and a signal that ROUTES beats a signal that REFUSES, because routing tells the session what to do next while a refusal only tells it to try again.

The name is the specification -- a model that never read this skill still knows what is wanted, which is the whole reason not to call it CROSS_CHECK or VERIFY. REQUIRED SHAPE: SECOND_MEASUREMENT: <the second quantity, named> = <its value>; <agrees|disagrees> with <the first claim>. WHY THIS FIELD AND NOT MORE PROSE: every catch of this shift came from measuring a SECOND, DIFFERENT quantity and comparing, never from reading one artifact harder -- a self-test fixture asserting ALLOWED while the code BLOCKED, a green 6-of-6 tally over a proto that had lost two of three functions (caught by counting function names in both files), a machine-token rule that passed any report containing a date (caught by inputs the author had not written), two scorers returning 100 and 69 for one skill. (B) STOP GATE, the load-bearing half: harness-agent-brief-guard step 17 already records the owner's reasoning that a brief is ephemeral and dies with its dispatch, so a protection written only into brief text depends on the dispatcher remembering it that day -- a Stop check fires at every turn-end regardless of who wrote the brief. THE ANTI-THEATRE CHECK, which is what stops the field becoming a ritual: the value must be a DIFFERENT quantity, not a restatement of the first. The Stop guard already ships an overlap detector -- the one refusing an EMERGENCY_ACTION that shares fewer than three meaningful words with KNOWN_BUGS -- and this needs the SAME machinery at OPPOSITE polarity: refuse when SECOND_MEASUREMENT overlaps the primary claim too HEAVILY, because high overlap means the same measurement was written twice. ACCEPT AN HONEST DISAGREES: a report whose second measurement CONTRADICTS the first is the most valuable report the fleet can produce and must pass, loudly -- if the gate only accepts agreement it has taught the fleet to measure until the numbers match, which manufactures the exact dishonesty it exists to catch.
